import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/data/invaded_niche_pathways.csv')

# Check the unique habitat types
unique_habitats = df['habitat'].unique()
print("Unique habitat types:", unique_habitats)

# Group the data by habitat and calculate the mean of 'n.gard'
grouped_data = df.groupby('habitat')['n.gard'].mean().reset_index()

# Plot the data
sns.barplot(x='habitat', y='n.gard', data=grouped_data)
plt.title('Prevalence of Non-Native Plants Introduced via Gardening by Habitat Type')
plt.xlabel('Habitat Type')
plt.ylabel('Prevalence (n.gard)')
plt.show()

# Display the grouped data
grouped_data

import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.formula.api import ols

# Load the dataset with corrected column names
df = pd.read_csv('/data/invaded_niche_pathways.csv', sep='\t')
df.columns = df.columns.str.replace('"', '').str.split('\t').str[0]

# Perform ANOVA
model = ols('n.gard ~ C(habitat)', data=df).fit()
anova_table = sm.stats.anova_lm(model, typ=2)
anova_table

import pandas as pd
import scipy.stats as stats

# Load the dataset with corrected column names
df = pd.read_csv('/data/invaded_niche_pathways.csv', sep='\t')
df.columns = df.columns.str.replace('"', '').str.split('\t').str[0]

# Group the data by habitat and extract 'n.gard' values
groups = [df[df['habitat'] == habitat]['n.gard'] for habitat in df['habitat'].unique()]

# Perform Kruskal-Wallis H-test
h_statistic, p_value = stats.kruskal(*groups)
h_statistic, p_value
